tool_schemas.name: get_version
tool_schemas.description: Returns the Home Assistant core version string currently recorded in the local mirror (for example, "2025.3.0"). Raises UNAVAILABLE if the mirror has not been initialized/synced yet or cannot read the stored version.

tool_schemas.name: get_entity
tool_schemas.description: Returns the current mirrored state for the given entity_id, optionally filtered to the requested fields, or the full object when detailed=true. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if entity_id is missing/invalid or if fields contains unsupported selectors, and NOT_FOUND if the entity_id does not exist in the mirror. Raises UNAVAILABLE if the mirror is not ready to serve reads (for example, before an initial sync completes).

tool_schemas.name: entity_action
tool_schemas.description: Performs the requested control action (on/off/toggle) for the given entity_id via Home Assistant and returns Home Assistant’s service-call response, recording the attempt and outcome in the audit trail. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if action is not one of on/off/toggle or if required inputs are missing, NOT_FOUND if the entity_id is unknown in the mirror, and FORBIDDEN if the caller is not authorized to issue control actions. Raises CONFLICT if the entity cannot accept the requested transition (for example, toggle/on/off is not supported for that entity), and UNAVAILABLE if Home Assistant cannot be reached to execute the action.

tool_schemas.name: list_entities
tool_schemas.description:
Get a list of Home Assistant entities with optional filtering

Args:
    domain: Optional domain to filter by (e.g., 'light', 'switch', 'sensor')
    search_query: Optional search term to filter entities by name, id, or attributes
                 (Note: Does not support wildcards. To get all entities, leave this empty)
    limit: Maximum number of entities to return (default: 100)
    fields: Optional list of specific fields to include in each entity
    detailed: If True, returns all entity fields without filtering

Returns:
    A list of entity dictionaries with lean formatting by default

Examples:
    domain="light" - get all lights
    search_query="kitchen", limit=20 - search entities
    domain="sensor", detailed=True - full sensor details

Best Practices:
    - Use lean format (default) for most operations
    - Prefer domain filtering over no filtering
    - For domain overviews, use domain_summary_tool instead of list_entities
    - Only request detailed=True when necessary for full attribute inspection
    - To get all entity types/domains, use list_entities without a domain filter, 
      then extract domains from entity_ids

tool_schemas.name: search_entities_tool
tool_schemas.description:
Search for entities matching a query string

Args:
    query: The search query to match against entity IDs, names, and attributes.
          (Note: Does not support wildcards. To get all entities, leave this blank or use list_entities tool)
    limit: Maximum number of results to return (default: 20)

Returns:
    A dictionary containing search results and metadata:
    - count: Total number of matching entities found
    - results: List of matching entities with essential information
    - domains: Map of domains with counts (e.g. {"light": 3, "sensor": 2})
    
Examples:
    query="temperature" - find temperature entities
    query="living room", limit=10 - find living room entities
    query="", limit=500 - list all entity types

tool_schemas.name: domain_summary_tool
tool_schemas.description:
Get a summary of entities in a specific domain

Args:
    domain: The domain to summarize (e.g., 'light', 'switch', 'sensor')
    example_limit: Maximum number of examples to include for each state

Returns:
    A dictionary containing:
    - total_count: Number of entities in the domain
    - state_distribution: Count of entities in each state
    - examples: Sample entities for each state
    - common_attributes: Most frequently occurring attributes
    
Examples:
    domain="light" - get light summary
    domain="climate", example_limit=5 - climate summary with more examples
Best Practices:
    - Use this before retrieving all entities in a domain to understand what's available

tool_schemas.name: system_overview
tool_schemas.description: Returns a computed overview of the mirrored Home Assistant system, including total_entities plus per-domain counts, optional state distributions, and up to limit_per_domain sample entities (domain_samples). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if limit_per_domain is negative or if any boolean flags are not valid booleans. Raises UNAVAILABLE if the mirror is not ready or contains no synchronized entity index yet.

limit_per_domain.description: Maximum number of sample entities to include per domain (used for domain_samples).

include_attributes.description: If true, include common attributes summary per domain.

include_state_distributions.description: If true, include per-domain state distribution counts.

tool_schemas.name: list_automations
tool_schemas.description: Lists automation records from the local mirror, optionally filtered by status, and returns either full objects (detailed=true) or only the requested fields per automation; if limit is provided, results are truncated to that maximum (no pagination token is produced). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if limit is negative, status is not one of active/removed, or requested fields are not supported. Raises UNAVAILABLE if the mirror has not been synced and automation data is not available.

limit.description: Maximum number of automations to return (default behavior is to return all if omitted).

fields.description: Optional list of fields to include for each automation (e.g. ['entity_id','state','alias']).

detailed.description: If true, return full automation objects without field filtering.

tool_schemas.name: restart_ha
tool_schemas.description: Requests a Home Assistant restart and returns the restart operation result, recording the reason (if provided) and outcome in the audit log. Raises FORBIDDEN if the caller is not authorized to restart Home Assistant, VALIDATION_ERROR if timeout_s is invalid (for example, negative), and CONFLICT if a restart is already in progress or the system refuses repeated restart requests. Raises UNAVAILABLE if Home Assistant cannot be reached to accept the restart command.

reason.description: Optional human-readable reason to record in the operation/audit log.

timeout_s.description: Optional timeout in seconds to wait for restart call completion.

tool_schemas.name: call_service_tool
tool_schemas.description: Calls an arbitrary Home Assistant service for the given domain and service name, passing through the optional data object, and returns Home Assistant’s service-call response while auditing the request and outcome. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if domain/service are missing or malformed or if data is not an object, FORBIDDEN if the caller is not authorized to use low-level service access, and NOT_FOUND if the domain/service does not exist. Raises UNAVAILABLE if Home Assistant cannot be reached or the call cannot be executed.

tool_schemas.name: get_history
tool_schemas.description: Returns recent mirrored state history for entity_id over the last hours, including the requested entity_id and a time-ordered list of state records with timestamps. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if hours is not a positive integer or entity_id is invalid, and NOT_FOUND if the entity_id does not exist in the mirror. Raises UNAVAILABLE if the history index is not available (for example, before history sync completes).

tool_schemas.name: get_error_log
tool_schemas.description:
Get the Home Assistant error log for troubleshooting

Returns:
    A dictionary containing:
    - log_text: The full error log text
    - error_count: Number of ERROR entries found
    - warning_count: Number of WARNING entries found
    - integration_mentions: Map of integration names to mention counts
    - error: Error message if retrieval failed
    
Examples:
    Returns errors, warnings count and integration mentions
Best Practices:
    - Use this tool when troubleshooting specific Home Assistant errors
    - Look for patterns in repeated errors
    - Pay attention to timestamps to correlate errors with events
    - Focus on integrations with many mentions in the log

max_lines.description: Maximum number of log lines to return from the error log (most recent lines).

since.description: Only include log entries at or after this timestamp (ISO 8601).

include_text.description: If true, include the raw log_text in the response; if false, return only counts and summaries.

tool_schemas.name: sync_instance
tool_schemas.description: Triggers a sync from Home Assistant into the local mirror for the active instance (entities, automations, and optionally recent history), upserting by instance/entity identifiers and recording an operation_logs audit row for the run. Refuses with UNAVAILABLE if the HA instance cannot be reached, and FORBIDDEN if the caller is not authorized to initiate a sync.

include_entities.description: If true, refresh the entities mirror from HA.

include_automations.description: If true, refresh the automations mirror from HA.

history_hours.description: If provided, ingest entity history for the last N hours (1..168). Null disables history ingestion.

source.description: Source label stored for any ingested history rows.

full_refresh.description: If true, re-index all entities/automations even if last_synced_at is recent.

tool_schemas.name: update_instance
tool_schemas.description: Updates writable fields for the active Home Assistant instance (for example name/base_url/token_ref) and/or drives allowed status transitions (active/degraded/offline/disabled). Refuses with VALIDATION_ERROR for invalid fields or illegal status transitions, and UNAVAILABLE if no instance exists.

name.description: Human-friendly name for this HA instance.

base_url.description: Base URL of the Home Assistant instance (e.g., http://homeassistant.local:8123).

token_ref.description: Reference to stored HA token/credential used by the backend to call HA (not the raw secret).

status.description: Set instance lifecycle status; must follow allowed transitions.

tool_schemas.name: list_operation_logs
tool_schemas.description: Lists audit-trail operation logs recorded by Hass-MCP with filtering by status, tool_name, entity_id, and time range, returning newest-first results. Refuses with VALIDATION_ERROR for invalid filters or pagination parameters, and FORBIDDEN if the caller is not allowed to view audit logs.

tool_name.description: Filter by tool name that produced the log row.

entity_id.description: Filter by Home Assistant entity_id associated with the operation (if any).

since.description: Only include logs with created_at >= since.

until.description: Only include logs with created_at <= until.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return (1..500).

offset.description: Number of rows to skip before returning results (>=0).

metadata.name: Hass-MCP
metadata.description: This backend stores a local, queryable mirror of a Home Assistant instance: its entities, recent state history, automations, and diagnostic logs, plus an audit trail of control actions issued through the MCP tools. Core workflows include syncing HA state into the mirror, serving filtered/searchable
